title: Coherent full-root source descent on common coefficient charts
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-regular-scheme], let $D=\bigcup_{a\in A}D_a$ be a reduced strict normal crossings divisor with finitely many components [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and put $W=Y\setminus D$. Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Assume that on every strict henselization at a geometric point, with parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ cutting out the branches of $D$, $L$ becomes constant on the inverse-limit cover of the complement obtained by adjoining compatible $n$th roots of all $t_i$ for every $n$ prime to $p$. This is the meaning of tame here; with no branches the cover is the identity. This is strict-local Kummer tameness [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module]. Write $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$, an ordinary tensor, for $F=E,\Omega$.
For any $J\subseteq A$, put $S_J=(\bigcap_{d\in J}D_d)\setminus\bigcup_{d\notin J}D_d$ with reduced structure and inclusion $s_J:S_J\to Y$. There are affine etale charts $B_\alpha\to Y\setminus\bigcup_{d\notin J}D_d$ with equations $t_d$ for $d\in J$, affine pro-etale $U_\alpha\to B_\alpha$, and a pro-etale covering $v_\alpha:T_\alpha=U_\alpha\times_Y S_J\to S_J$, together with compatible roots of unity. Let
$$\mathcal T_\alpha=\varprojlim_{(n,p)=1}\operatorname{Spec}_{U_\alpha}(\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}[x_d]_{d\in J}/(x_d^n-t_d)_d),\qquad \mathcal T_\alpha^\circ=\mathcal T_\alpha\times_YW,$$
with power transitions. There is a deck-equivariant lisse extension $\mathcal N_\alpha$ of the actual pullback of $L$ to $\mathcal T_\alpha$, with boundary module $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,E}$ for a finite-dimensional continuous $E$-representation $M_\alpha$ of $G_J=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^J$. Here $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_m\mathbf Z/q^m\mathbf Z$. Its ordinary extension to $C_\Omega$ is lisse, restricts to the actual pullback of $L_\Omega$, and has boundary $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,\Omega}$, so the charts, roots and cover are simultaneous for both fields. Through the chosen roots of unity, $\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ\to U_\alpha\times_YW$ is a pro-etale covering and a $G_J$-torsor for the root deck action.
Let $c:W\hookrightarrow Y$. For $P=G_J^n$, the $n$th term of the root-cover Cech nerve is $\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ[P]$, where $X[P]$ is the inverse limit of finite disjoint copies of $X$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects]. Let $q_{\alpha,n}:\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ[P]\to U_\alpha$ be structural and $e_\alpha:T_\alpha\hookrightarrow U_\alpha$. Write $\mathcal N_{\alpha,E}=\mathcal N_\alpha$ and $\mathcal N_{\alpha,\Omega}$ for its ordinary extension to $C_\Omega$. The restriction-of-sections comparisons of [lem-sfb-root-tower-boundary-acyclicity], applied with $U=U_\alpha$, $s=e_\alpha$, $v_P=q_{\alpha,n}$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal N_{\alpha,F}$, give an isomorphism of coherent cosimplicial derived module objects
$$e_\alpha^*R(q_{\alpha,n})_*(\mathcal N_{\alpha,F}|_{\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ[P]}[0])\cong p_{T_\alpha}^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[G_J^n],M_{\alpha,F}).$$
The free internal module $C_F[P]$ is left adjoint to the forgetful functor to condensed sets and internal Hom is right adjoint to module tensor, derived in its second variable. The comparisons identify every face and degeneracy, including the action face as a morphism on the entire profinite family. They retain the augmented compatible first-quadrant resolution, with finite diagonals and differential $d_{\rm Cech}+(-1)^n d_{\rm res}$. Their totalization gives the augmentation-normalized derived isomorphism
$$\alpha_{\alpha,F}:(s_Jv_\alpha)^*Rc_*L_F[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}p_{T_\alpha}^*\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}B_F^n(M_\alpha)\cong p_{T_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_J}(M_{\alpha,F}),$$
where $B_F^n(M_\alpha)=R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_F}(C_F[G_J^n],M_{\alpha,F})$ with the inhomogeneous group bar maps [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. These comparisons are natural in maps of the supplied equivariant extensions and in pro-etale restrictions of the charts. No scalar/direct-image comparison is asserted to be invertible. The assertion includes empty strata, $J=\varnothing$ and rank zero. The coherent comparisons hold for any supplied charts and equivariant extensions having the displayed properties, in particular on common refinements chosen for a morphism. Sites are small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; continuous representations and their condensed actions use [def-sfb-norm-continuous-monodromy-data, def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and all derived categories are the ordinary ones [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

proof.text: Apply the tame-root extension theorem with $I=J$. Its hypotheses are precisely the stated regular SNC pair, finite-rank lisse $L$ and strict-local Kummer triviality; it gives the affine charts, stratum covering, compatible roots, actual equivariant extension $\mathcal N_\alpha$, continuous boundary representation $M_\alpha$, and pro-etale root torsor. Denote its root tower by $\mathcal T_\alpha$ and its stratum by $T_\alpha$, to match the item. No assertion about higher images is taken from that theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text: On a finite-free trivialization, ordinary scalar extension sends $C_E^d$ to $C_\Omega^d$. Thus $\mathcal N_{\alpha,\Omega}$ is lisse and restricts to the pullback of $L_\Omega$. Choose an $E$-basis of $M_\alpha$. The identities $C(P,E^d)=C(P,E)^d$ and $C(P,\Omega^d)=C(P,\Omega)^d$ identify its boundary with $p_{T_\alpha}^*M_{\alpha,\Omega}$. Finite sums and the balanced tensor formula commute with inverse image. The action matrix is extended entrywise; its multiplication law and its continuity persist under the continuous inclusion $E\to\Omega$. Consequently both fields use the very same charts, roots and cover; flatness of the coefficient inclusion is unnecessary.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text:
Write $X=\mathcal T_\alpha^\circ$, $U^\circ=U_\alpha\times_YW$, and $G=G_J$. Iterating the torsor isomorphism gives the nerve coordinates
$$(x,g_1,\ldots,g_n)\longmapsto(x,g_1x,g_2g_1x,\ldots,g_n\cdots g_1x).$$
The inverse successively takes the unique group element carrying one lift to the next; this is a morphism of schemes because it is obtained by repeated base change of the supplied torsor isomorphism. Deleting the first vertex gives $(g_1x,g_2,\ldots,g_n)$; deleting an interior vertex multiplies its two adjacent ratios; deleting the last drops $g_n$. Repeating a vertex inserts $1$. These formulas are identities on the whole relative profinite schemes, obtained from the torsor action and associativity, and also show compatibility with restrictions. The coefficient identification at the changed first vertex is the supplied equivariant identification, not an independently chosen trivialization.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text:
The coefficient-section localization theorem identifies $U_\alpha$ and $U^\circ$ with the appropriate pro-etale slices. Apply derived slice localization to $c$ and $U_\alpha\to Y$; it identifies the restriction of $Rc_*L_F[0]$ with $Rc_{\alpha,*}(L_F|_{U^\circ}[0])$, preserving the adjunction normalization. Apply augmented derived Cech image descent to $c_\alpha:U^\circ\hookrightarrow U_\alpha$, the cover $X\to U^\circ$, and $e_\alpha:T_\alpha\hookrightarrow U_\alpha$. This gives
$$(s_Jv_\alpha)^*Rc_*L_F[0]\cong\operatorname{Tot}_n e_\alpha^*R(q_{\alpha,n})_*(\mathcal N_{\alpha,F}|_{X[G^n]}[0]).$$
The cover is on $U^\circ$, before applying $e_\alpha^*$; it is never base changed to the empty open on the stratum. All inputs are degree-zero modules, all sites and the nerve index are small, and Cartesian coefficient inverse images are exact. Descent supplies a compatible first-quadrant model and the restriction-of-sections augmentation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text:
For each $P=G^n$, apply root-tower boundary acyclicity with its $U=U_\alpha$, $S=T_\alpha$, $T=\mathcal T_\alpha$, $s=e_\alpha$, $v_P=q_{\alpha,n}$ and the supplied $\mathcal N_{\alpha,F}$. The hypotheses are the same SNC chart, affine pro-etale $U_\alpha$, finite-rank lisse extension, and its specified finite-dimensional $E$-boundary model; for $\Omega$ use step 2. It gives the displayed term isomorphism to $p_{T_\alpha}^*B_F^n(M_\alpha)$. Its parameter naturality gives the interior, final and degeneracy maps of step 3. For the first face use its stronger clause for continuous families of deck automorphisms with the equivariant action: over the whole $G$-parameter object, changing the first lift gives
$$(d^0b)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1b(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1}).$$
The other formulas are $d^ib(g)=b(g_1,\ldots,g_{i+1}g_i,\ldots,g_{n+1})$ and $d^{n+1}b(g)=b(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$; $G$ is commutative, so this is the usual ordered inhomogeneous bar convention. These are family identities, not a check at individual geometric points.

proof.text: Retain compatible resolutions in step 5 as follows. Use the nonnegative Cech column model for the geometric nerve. For the boundary comparison use the cospan consisting of the puncture unit on the full tower, restriction of full-tower sections along the zero-root map, and free-generator evaluation on $T_\alpha[P]$. The first arrow is the open unit of puncture invariance; the middle arrow is precisely the normalized counit adjunct of integral-fibre specialization, whose geometry is supplied by the integral nil-fibre theorem; the last is the parameter-functions comparison. Thus these are specified natural units, counits and evaluation maps before passing to derived objects. They are not isomorphisms selected solely in the homotopy category. Use their naturality for simultaneous parameter maps and module actions to form the whole simplex-indexed cospan; the formulas of step 3 give its operators.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text: To resolve that cospan simultaneously, use the Grothendieck property of small ringed-site module categories, functorial injective embeddings, and the bounded-below functorial resolution, with lower bound zero. Apply the same resolution functor to every coefficient complex and every arrow, including the maps over profinite parameter slices; functoriality preserves their composition equations. For the function end use free-generator evaluation: its simultaneous parameter and linear-map identity identifies the action maps as well as the parameter maps. Canonical resolution comparisons assemble on the entire indexing diagram by derived resolution naturality. Hence the cospan of step 6 is represented by a common nonnegative resolution diagram, with column quasi-isomorphisms, preserving every face and degeneracy. The puncture arrow is inverted only after localization. Totalize its two arrows; column comparison makes both totals invertible. This supplies the coherent comparison used here, without inferring a total map from independently commuting triangles in a triangulated category.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text: The resolved nerve and bar differentials commute with the resolution differential, since all their operators are chain maps. Set the total differential to $d_{\rm Cech}+(-1)^n d_{\rm res}$. In degree $r$ only $n+q=r$ with $n,q\ge0$ occurs, so exact $p_{T_\alpha}^*$ commutes with this total by its finite-biproduct identifications. Compose step 4 with the total comparison of steps 6-7 and then with the inverse of the internal derived-invariant bar isomorphism. This is the asserted $\alpha_{\alpha,F}$. The descent augmentation in Cech degree zero is actual restriction of sections. At $P=*$ the boundary comparison is the inverse of the open unit, and free-generator evaluation is the identity. Thus the composite has exactly the stated augmentation normalization; the bar theorem uses inclusion of invariants, with no rescaling or arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text: For a map of supplied equivariant extensions, use that actual map in every column and in the coefficient action face. Parameter-family naturality of the boundary comparison and module naturality of the bar comparison give the resulting square. Apply the current augmentation-naturality theorem to $f=c_\alpha$, $K=L_F|_{U^\circ}$ and the epimorphism $X\to U^\circ$, using the canonical coherent element-site model supplied in step 6. A covering refinement is another epimorphism, as that theorem now explicitly requires. Its resolution comparisons preserve the whole augmented total map and commute with those refinement restrictions. Apply exact $e_\alpha^*$ to these identities; finite diagonals identify the resulting total complexes. For the counit normalization, first project the total to Cech column zero. There the map is $f_*(\eta_I)$; the identity adjoint transpose belongs to $\eta_I:I\to v_{0*}v_0^*I$ before applying $f_*$, not to a map of modules on the target. This is exactly the degree-zero normalization used in step 8. Pro-etale chart restrictions use the same section restrictions and the boundary comparison's base-change clause. Hence the construction applies to any supplied charts and their supplied common refinements. Both fields use the same geometry; no scalar/direct-image comparison is inverted.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent expansion of the open-image calculation: coherent full-root source descent

proof.text: If $S_J=\varnothing$, use the empty cover and the zero derived category on the empty stratum. If $J=\varnothing$, the tower and group are identities and the chosen charts trivialize $L$; the augmented identity nerve is split and its normalized positive degrees are zero. The comparison reduces to that trivialization in degree zero. For rank zero every module, column and total is zero. All constructions above therefore include exactly the stated edge cases.
